trade.name: Trade agreement
trade.benefits: Letters travel both ways: each side hears the other’s news, and trust grows by 1 a day.
trade.breach: Ending it early is a broken promise others hear about.

passage.name: Right of passage
passage.benefits: Your armed parties may cross their frontier land (never their protected core).
passage.obligations: Your soldiers must not stop or fight there.
passage.breach: A broken promise, and armed entry becomes an incident again.

nonAggression.name: Non-aggression pact
nonAggression.benefits: Both sides worry less about each other’s troops.
nonAggression.obligations: No war between you while it lasts.
nonAggression.breach: Declaring war or ending it early is a serious broken promise.

defensiveAlliance.name: Defensive alliance
defensiveAlliance.benefits: Allies share what they learn, and may answer calls for aid.
defensiveAlliance.obligations: Answer your ally’s call for aid if they are attacked (you decide how). It does not bind them to your offensive wars.
defensiveAlliance.breach: Refusing a call for aid costs trust; ending it early is a broken promise.

truce.name: Truce
truce.benefits: Fighting stops while terms are discussed.
truce.breach: Attacking during a truce is a grave broken promise.

peace.name: Peace treaty
peace.benefits: Ends a war; any land transfers written into it take effect.
